rows.title: nuclear-atlas — Rules
rows.summary: extension; closing the page leaves both going, and a notice says when an order ends.
body: - `chat.ts` has no `vscode` import.
- The work does not belong to the page: the members answer through the chat service, and an order is a run of the
extension; closing the page leaves both going, and a notice says when an order ends.
- The conversation is Nuclear Chat's (`.nuclear/chat/` of the project); the page never holds the service's token.
- Nuclear Atlas never calls a model by itself: questions go to the general agent, orders to Nuclear Builder.
- The decision: ADR-platform-0003

body: - Ask about your project and hand off small work without the code leaving the machine.

rows.title: Nuclear Builder (`nuclear-builder`)
rows.summary: The pipeline tool of the editors, Nuclear Builder, the software factory (spec 011): a spec goes through the stations analysis, design, tests first, code, quality and delivery on the developer's machine, each worked by a role of the user's team (a local agent or a provider), and every step shows…
body: The pipeline tool of the editors, **Nuclear Builder**, the software factory (spec 011): a spec goes through the
stations analysis, design, tests first, code, quality and delivery on the developer's machine, each worked by a role
of the user's team (a local agent or a provider), and every step shows who did it (the role, the employee, the
provider and model, the shell, you). It is a tool of the Nuclear workspace in VS Code
(`Ctrl+Alt+P`), a tool window in Android Studio / IntelliJ (`Alt+Shift+P`) and the `nuclear-builder` command in a
terminal or a CI job. It needs the Smart Graph and the Nuclear Developer running.

rows.title: Nuclear Builder (`nuclear-builder`) — Rules
rows.summary: a shell; an API key lives only in the keyring and never reaches a log, a run file or an error.
body: - A run is `.nuclear/builder/runs/<id>.json`, saved on every step: every editor and the command draw that same file.
- The factory's adapters render a role in a temporary folder of the run, never in the user's files; no agent gets
a shell; an API key lives only in the keyring and never reaches a log, a run file or an error.
- Commands are data (`.nuclear/builder.json`): the shell runs nothing that is not there.
- The local agents only ever see Nuclear and the platform, never a dialect's language.
- No Nuclear Builder for Zed (decided by the user).
- The decision behind the pipeline is ADR-platform-0003, the software factory ADR-platform-0005 (its teams amended by ADR-platform-0010), the workbench and
the chat ADR-platform-0006; the strategies, ADR-developer-0001; the generators, ADR-codegen-0001.

rows.title: Nuclear Builder (`nuclear-builder`) — Rules
rows.summary: alive (decided by the user: the least memory and the fewest problems of compatibility).
body: - The editors run the set-up as a process (`nuclear-builder setup ...`), one call per action: no process of it stays
alive (decided by the user: the least memory and the fewest problems of compatibility). Its JSON is the contract
of the pages.
- The chat is Nuclear Chat (`docs/02-architecture/chat.md`): the service runs a member's `nuclear-builder member
--events` per answer; a member writes only through the factory's tools, never a role's files, and a spec only when
the user accepts its draft. The extension holds the service's token; a page never does.
- The editors run the line as a process, one per run (`nuclear-builder run|retry|restart … --events`, the contract of
`docs/02-architecture/engine.md`); `runs.ts` and `support.ts` never import `vscode`.
- **The UI is only a UI** (ADR-platform-0009): every action is a command of `nuclear-builder` and a tool of
`nuclear-builder mcp` ([actions.md](docs/02-architecture/actions.md)); a new button costs its command, its tool, its
row there and its test first. A tool never confirms money (`waiting: spending`) nor destroys or acts in the user's
name (`needsUser`); merging is never a tool.
- The page only draws and answers. A run belongs to the extension (`driveRun`'s processes, module-level): closing the
page or switching tools leaves it running; Nuclear Atlas's `/task` runs through it too.

rows.title: Nuclear Builder (`nuclear-builder`) — Where the code is
rows.summary: Where the code is
body: | File | What it is |

| `setup.nuc` | the set-up: this machine, the profiles and how each sits on it, the ports, the services at login, the steps (the commands they run say each line as it comes, a Python one too: `PYTHONUNBUFFERED`); no editor |

| `cli.nuc`, `terminal.nuc` | the `nuclear-builder` command: `setup` in a terminal and for the editors (`--plan --json`, `--events`, `--status --json`, `--restart`, `--set`), `team …` and `vault …` (JSON for the editors; `team screen`: the company screen in one call), `spec …` (with `accept`/`discard` of a draft), `member`, `chat-host`, `agents`, the line's commands of `line.nuc`; `member`, `chat-host` and `mcp` import their modules when they run (`lazy_imports` of `nuclear.toml` puts each import in its command's branch: the `mcp` library is 300 ms), so every other command starts in under 100 ms |

| `line.nuc` | `run`, `retry`, `restart`, `runs`, `checks`, `ci`, `export`, `line`: the factory in a terminal, a CI job, an editor's process (`--events`: JSON lines out, answers in) or apart (`--detach`); `run answer|stop|show|journal` |

| `factory.nuc` | the software factory's engine: the stations, the roles' steps, the strategy, the wiring, the repairs, the lead, the acceptance, the diagnosis, the gates, the checks, the money, the delivery |

rows.title: Nuclear Builder (`nuclear-builder`) — Where the code is
rows.summary: Where the code is
body: | `run.nuc` | the run file and its journal (`<id>.md`), the spec, the trace log, the owner's heartbeat, the ledger, the rollback, the recovery |

| `specs.nuc`, `spec_line.nuc` | the specs by component and layer (`specs/<component>/[<layer>/]<id>/`, `_global`): their folders, a run's `specPath`; `spec new`, `list`, `move`, `migrate`, a draft's `accept` and `discard` |

| `chat.nuc` | the factory's agent in a conversation, the base of `member.nuc`: its turn, its factory tools (the Builder's MCP tools; text blocks for the local member), what a tool asks of the user asked and applied, the role files' guard, its spending |

| `usage.nuc`, `metrics.nuc` | the reports (spec 017): the factory's ledger (`~/.config/nuclearlang/factory/ledger/<yyyy-mm>.jsonl`, one line per step, run and chat answer across projects; the lines of a write; the runs of before copied once) and `metrics … --json` (the tool `metrics`): the bill, throughput, cycle, burndown, flow, waiting, quality, people, indicators |

| `tools.nuc`, `mcp.nuc` | every action of the Builder as an agent's tool (`BuilderTools`, `applyForUser`, `projectRead`: a PDF, a `.pptx`, text) and `nuclear-builder mcp`, the Builder's MCP server (docs/02-architecture/actions.md) |

rows.summary: Where the code is
body: | `member.nuc` | Nuclear Chat's host (spec 013): `member --team --member <id> --events` (`--role`: the role's first member), a member's one answer (the chat's turn with the member's own prompt), and `chat-host --json`, every member (`<team>-<member id>`) and the channels of the project's team and the general agent `atlas` with its choices |
| `chat_agents.nuc` | `agents --json` (the tool `agents_list`): the agents a conversation can choose on this machine, the general agent's choices for the chat (spec 013 requirement 17) |

| `models.nuc` | `models --json` (the tool `models_list`): each provider's models from the provider (Claude Code's, `opencode models`, an API's list, Ollama's installed and pullable ones), this machine's memory, a local model's memory need and fit (fits, tight, too-big), the members' memory `warnings` of `team create`/`member add|update` (spec 011 req. 35) |
| `checks.nuc`, `preflight.nuc`, `ci.nuc` | the run's checks (`checks.json` in the spec's folder); *Check the connections*; the line (`.nuclear/builder.json`), its CI commands and files |
| `setup.json` | the data of the set-up: the requirements, the embeddings model, the profiles |
| `roles.nuc` | the software factory's five roles, its stations, where the roles' folders are, their rosters (with each employee's face and its thumbnail), the temperaments |

- **Nuclear** (`python` dialect, `nuclear.toml`): the set-up of the AI services, the `nuclear-builder` command, and
the software factory's teams, vault and providers.
`nuclear build .` writes `build/nuclear_builder`, packaged by `pyproject.toml` and installed in the AI archive
(`installer/release/ai-runtime.sh`). Its line's commands (`run`, `retry`, `restart`, `runs`, `checks`, `ci`,
`export`) run the software factory's engine, in Nuclear.
- **TypeScript**: the VS Code page, which runs the line as a process and draws its run file, compiled and bundled by
the VS Code extension (`src/`, `test/`, `extensions/vscode/tsconfig.json`); the JetBrains `build.sh` compiles
`jetbrains/src/` with the plugin.

rows.title: Nuclear Builder — How we made it
rows.summary: How we made it
body: - One of the four projects of the AI loop ([ADR-platform-0003](../../../docs/03-adr/0003-the-ai-loop.md)).
- A strategy per kind of request decides the stages ([ADR-developer-0001](../../../nuclear-agents/nuclear_developer/docs/03-adr/0001-a-strategy-for-each-kind-of-request.md)).

- The generators write first, the agents only what is left ([ADR-codegen-0001](../../../tools/code_generator/docs/03-adr/0001-the-generators-write-finished-code-the-agent-only-what-is-not-standard.md), [ADR-platform-0004](../../../docs/03-adr/0004-products-are-made-with-the-tools.md)).

- Claude leads by default: the local developer passes 41 or 42 of 42 single files (Sonnet 36) but one or two of three features (Sonnet three) ([the rounds](../../../nuclear-agents/nuclear_developer/docs/05-standards/testing.md)).
- A run is a file that survives a crash; one engine in TypeScript with no editor inside it.

rows.title: Nuclear Builder — Why
rows.summary: Why
body: - Work with AI starts from a spec and ends in tested, reviewed code, every step visible.
- Claude leads (plan, names, review); the local Nuclear Developer writes each piece, on your machine.
- The same pipeline runs on a server; the shell runs only what `.nuclear/builder.json` allows.

rows.title: Domain: spec, run, station, role, team
rows.summary: The Builder is the software factory of spec 011: one engine, written in Nuclear (`factory.nuc`, `run.nuc`), run by the editors and the terminal as the `nuclear-builder` process.
body: The Builder is the software factory of spec 011: one engine, written in Nuclear (`factory.nuc`, `run.nuc`), run by
the editors and the terminal as the `nuclear-builder` process.

rows.title: Domain: spec, run, station, role, team — How the work is split
rows.summary: So that the local 3B models only think the business logic: 1. Before anyone writes, the transpiler has written the project map; the agents read it instead of every file.
body: So that the local 3B models only think the business logic:
1. Before anyone writes, the transpiler has written the **project map**; the agents read it instead of every file.
2. **Design**: the generators write first what follows from the data (`nuclear gen resource`); the plan holds only
what is left.
3. **Tests first**: one test per acceptance criterion, with the names the plan gives.
4. **Code**: each piece at its place, checked by the compiler, each use case wired by `nuclear gen usecase`; the
errors left go back to the Developer, then to the lead.
5. **Quality**: every test runs; a failing test goes back told in Nuclear (`nuclear explain`), up to three rounds,
then to the lead. A station run again runs its role's checks again.

rows.title: Domain: spec, run, station, role, team — Invariants
rows.summary: the run's budget.
body: - The local agents only ever see Nuclear and the platform (backend, mobile, web), never Python, TypeScript or Dart.
- A spec needs at least one acceptance criterion.
- Nothing is guessed: a request that lacks a fact its strategy needs stops at the analysis, with the question.
- A bug's repair goes to the file the failure names, whoever wrote it, and never to the test.
- Two processes never run the same run.
- A file the user changed since the run wrote it is never undone.
- No paid call without the two confirmations (or `--confirm-spending` where the project allows it), and never over
the run's budget.
- Nothing is merged: DevOps opens a pull request, only after the user approves it.

rows.title: Domain: spec, run, station, role, team — The stations, in order
rows.summary: Analysis → Design → Tests first → Code → Quality → Delivery.
body: Analysis → Design → Tests first → Code → Quality → Delivery. The analysis names the strategy; a strategy may leave
stations out (each one says why). Artifacts and deploy are commands of the line (`nuclear-builder ci`), not stations.

rows.title: Domain: spec, run, station, role, team — Who works
rows.summary: The local analyst picks the strategy, the local diagnoser tells why a station failed, the local
body: | Who | Does | Does not |
| You | write the spec, choose the team, answer the gates, run and mark your checks, approve the delivery | write a piece here |
| Analyst | reads the spec as the client's request, makes the criteria checkable, asks what is missing | design or build |
| Architect | designs what the generators did not write, the plan of one-file pieces; the lead when the Developer is local | write every piece |
| Developer | the tests first, then the code; the local one (Nuclear Developer) through its planner, coder and tester on models of 3B at most | choose names, data or architecture |
| QA | the plan of checks (functional, non-functional, security, load), runs its own, writes the report | change the code |

| DevOps | the Delivery station: the definition of done, the user stories, the pull request after your approval; the CI, the deployments and environments, the containers, the monitoring, the secrets | merge, deploy to production or write a secret without you |
| Shell | runs the line's commands and the generators | run anything not in `.nuclear/builder.json` |
The local **analyst** picks the strategy, the local **diagnoser** tells why a station failed, the local
**documenter** writes the top of the journal.

rows.title: Vision — Problem
rows.summary: Work with AI agents should start from a spec and end in tested, reviewed code, on the developer's machine, with every step visible.
body: Work with AI agents should start from a spec and end in tested, reviewed code, on the developer's machine, with
every step visible. The same pipeline must be able to run on a server.

rows.title: Vision — The idea
rows.summary: A frontier model like Claude makes the decisions (the plan, the names, the review) and the local developer writes each piece.
body: A frontier model like Claude makes the decisions (the plan, the names, the review) and the local developer writes
each piece. A lead hands work to a junior the same way. What the junior cannot fix, Claude fixes and keeps as an
example, so the junior gets it right next time.

rows.title: Vision — The three pieces
rows.summary: The three pieces
body: | Piece | What it is | Project |

| Nuclear Smart Graph | A private library of the whole ecosystem, as cards on shelves: what it is for, how each thing is written, every kind, tool and error, what can and cannot be done, how each task is done, validated code. Plus the MCP server of NuclearLang for Claude Code, Codex or Cursor | `nuclear-graph-storage/`, `tools/mcp/` |

| Nuclear Developer | Local agents on 3B models: a coder, a tester, a security reviewer and a planner. They search the graph and check their answers with the compiler | `nuclear-agents/nuclear_developer/` |
| Nuclear Builder | The pipeline: a spec goes through its stages, and every step shows who did it | this project |

rows.title: Vision — Users
rows.summary: (the MCP server).
body: - A developer in VS Code (`Ctrl+Alt+P`) or Android Studio / IntelliJ (`Alt+Shift+P`).
- A terminal or a CI job: `nuclear-builder`.
- A frontier model over MCP: `developer_task` runs this pipeline with the local agents and answers the journal
([the MCP server](../../../../../tools/mcp/AGENTS.md)).

rows.title: Vision — What it does not do
rows.summary: What it does not do
body: - It does not run in Zed.
- The shell runs nothing that is not in `.nuclear/builder.json`.
- The agent stages do not run on a server: the server checks their result with the deterministic stages.
- The acceptance step informs; it never fails a run.

rows.title: Vision — Who leads, and why
rows.summary: The local developer is measured against Claude Sonnet on a bank of 45 tasks, 18 of them held out: 42 single files of every platform and 3 features of several files.
body: *Claude leads, the local developer writes* is the default; *Local agents only* is the other choice.
The local developer is measured against Claude Sonnet on a bank of 45 tasks, 18 of them held out: 42 single files of
every platform and 3 features of several files. On single files the local 3B coder passes 41 or 42 of the 42
(Sonnet 36). On whole features it is behind: it passes one or two of the three by itself, while Sonnet passes all
three. That is
why Claude leads by default: it plans and fixes, the local developer writes the pieces. The method, every round and
every task are in [the Developer's README](../../../../../nuclear-agents/nuclear_developer/README.md).

rows.title: The actions: every button is a command and a tool
rows.summary: ADR-platform-0009: the UI is only a UI.
body: ADR-platform-0009: the UI is only a UI. Every action of the Builder's page, the company screen and the Builder's
settings is a command of `nuclear-builder` (Nuclear, `--json`), and every command an agent may use is a tool of the
Builder's MCP server, `nuclear-builder mcp` (`tools.nuc`, `mcp.nuc`), with the same name and arguments. The page and
the agents are two clients of the same commands. A test holds the three together (`tests/test_tools.nuc`: every
tool is in this page and its command in the help; `test/editors.test.ts`: every message of the pages names a
command of this page).
**Who** says who may do it through a tool:

rows.title: The actions: every button is a command and a tool
rows.summary: "run", "spending": {roles, providers, budgetUsd}}` and the run waits.
body: - **anyone**: an agent does it by itself.
- **spending**: it may start a paid provider. The tool never confirms the money: it answers `{"waiting": "spending",
"run", "spending": {roles, providers, budgetUsd}}` and the run waits. The user confirms twice where they answer:
the editor's two modal questions (Resume on the page, spec 011 requirement 16) or the chat's two `ask` (the member
asks them, then `applyForUser("run_spending")` keeps the confirmation in the run and resumes it). *Force
confirmation* holds: only `--confirm-spending` is refused by it, never the user's own answers.
- **user**: it destroys, or it acts in the user's name. The tool answers `{"needsUser": {tool, input, question,
command}}` and changes nothing; the chat asks the user (`ask` of kind `confirm`) and applies it on a yes
(`applyForUser`); elsewhere the agent tells the user, who does it on the page or with the `command`.
- **host**: no tool. It belongs to the machine, the keyring or the editor.
Merging a pull request is never a tool, nor a command.

body: A run is started by the page (`run … --events`, its process the extension's) or apart (`run … --detach`, an agent's
`run_start`: no stdin, so it waits at its first question, which `run answer` answers). A question is answered on
stdin or through `.nuclear/builder/runs/<id>.answer.json`, which `run answer` and `run stop` write for the process
that waits on it (`eventAnswer`: stdin read by a thread, the file looked at twice a second). The spending is never

A spec goes through the stations, each worked by a member of its role in the run's team.

rows.title: The engine — The editors' side
rows.summary: form's whole markdown on stdin); the tree is `spec list --json` (overview.md, *The page*).
body: - **VS Code** (`src/runs.ts`, `src/panel.ts`): a spec is placed and written by `spec new … --stdin --json` (the
form's whole markdown on stdin); the tree is `spec list --json` (overview.md, *The page*). `LineRun` is one run's process; `driveRun` keeps them by run id, at the
extension's level (a closed page, another tool or Nuclear Atlas's `/task` share them). The run file is watched by
its `stat` (it is replaced atomically) and drawn at most ten times a second. A `spending` ask is answered by the
editor's two modal questions (`vscode/src/spending.ts`), a `gate` or `checks` ask by the page; an answer given to a
run that ended waiting starts `run --resume <id>` and is given again when the same question comes (`answerRun`).
`resumeOrphans`, on activation, runs `retry <id>` for every run of this engine that was `running` with no live
owner (`nuclear.builder.resumeInterrupted`). *Stop* closes the stdin of a run that waits (it keeps waiting) and
sends SIGINT to one that works (its working steps fail, what they wrote is undone).
- **JetBrains** (`NuclearBuilder.java`): the same contract, its questions as dialogs.

rows.title: The engine — The process contract
rows.summary: provider does (`text`, `tool`, `tool-result`, `cost`, `tokens`, `retry`, `trace`); `{"type": "ask", "id", "kind", "question", …}` when it needs the user (`kind`: `gate` with its `station` and `documents`, and at the Analysis's gate the analysis's open `questions`; `spending` with its `providers`…
body: - **stdout**: one JSON object per line. `{"type": "event", "step": "<step id>", "event": {…}}` for what a
provider does (`text`, `tool`, `tool-result`, `cost`, `tokens`, `retry`, `trace`); `{"type": "ask", "id", "kind",
"question", …}` when it needs the user (`kind`: `gate` with its `station` and `documents`, and at the Analysis's
gate the analysis's open `questions`; `spending` with its `providers` and `budgetUsd`; `checks` with the `checks`
file); `{"type": "done", "status", "costUsd"}` at the end.
The run file changes with every step: the editors draw it, not the events.
- **stdin**: one JSON object per line, the answer to the last `ask`: `{"answer": "approve"}` (or `"yes"`),
`{"answer": "change", "text": "…"}` at a gate, `{"answer": "no"}` / `{"answer": "stop"}`. stdin closed or an empty
line: the run stops with `status: "waiting"` and `waiting` set; `run --resume <id>` asks again.
- **Exit code**: 0 passed, 1 failed, 2 a wrong call, 3 waiting for the user.
- Without `--events`, the same run in a terminal: a line per step that ended, the questions asked there (no terminal:
the run waits).
A member of Nuclear Chat (`nuclear-builder member --events`) answers with the same shape of events, one process per
answer: [chat.md](chat.md).

`<id>.log` (JSON lines); the process beats every 10 s (`owner`), a beat older than 45 s or a dead process on this
machine is an orphaned run; every file a step changes goes to the ledger (`writes`: the text before, the digest
after, the lines added and removed), found by comparing the project's files before and after the step; what a failed step wrote is undone, a
file changed since is kept and named; an orphaned run is recovered (its running steps failed, their files undone,
`interrupted`, with the `stepId` it was in) and goes on from that step; a retry from a station moves the steps from

commands, accept, checks, work, gate); a part that ended is kept in `stages[].phases`, so a run that waited goes on in its
station after them.

rows.title: Architecture of Nuclear Builder
rows.summary: The engine is the software factory, in Nuclear: `line.nuc` → `factory.nuc` → the adapters of the team's providers (providers.md), with the teams and the vault of teams-and-vault.md and the process contract of engine.md.
body: The engine is the software factory, in Nuclear: `line.nuc` → `factory.nuc` → the adapters of the team's providers
([providers.md](providers.md)), with the teams and the vault of [teams-and-vault.md](teams-and-vault.md) and the
process contract of [engine.md](engine.md). Every editor runs it as a process and draws the run file it writes.

rows.title: Architecture of Nuclear Builder — The commands (`line.nuc`, `cli.nuc`)
rows.summary: The commands (`line.nuc`, `cli.nuc`)
body: | Command | What it does |
| `nuclear-builder run [spec.md] [--team <id>] [--events] [--confirm-spending] [--force-confirm]` | the stations of the factory; no file = the spec changed last |
| `nuclear-builder run … --detach` | the run in a process of its own, no stdin (an agent's tool): `{run, detached, log}` (`.nuclear/builder/runs/<id>.out`) |
| `nuclear-builder run --resume <id> [--events]` | a run that waits goes on (it asks its question again) |
| `nuclear-builder run answer <id> --answer … [--text …]` | the answer to the question a run waits on: to its process (the answer file) or the run goes on with it; never the spending |
| `nuclear-builder run stop\|show\|journal <id>` | a run's process stopped (a run that asks waits); its file; its journal |
| `nuclear-builder retry <run> [--from <station>]` | a run again from the station that did not pass, or from a station |
| `nuclear-builder restart <run>` | every station again from scratch (a run of the earlier engine too) |
| `nuclear-builder checks <run> [list \| on \| off \| add \| mark] --json` | the run's checks (the console) |
| `nuclear-builder ci [stage...]` | the deterministic stages of `.nuclear/builder.json` |
| `nuclear-builder export github\|gitlab\|bitbucket` | writes the CI file |
| `nuclear-builder runs [--json]` | the runs of this project |

body: - **Context**: the project in the middle (its spec, its progress, its time and cost); you on its left; the team's members who work the run

(`.nuclear/builder/runs/*.json`, newest first: the team, the cost, what it waits for) → stations (the role, the

body: The page writes nothing itself (ADR-platform-0009, [actions.md](actions.md); `src/actions.ts` names the command of
each of its messages). A spec is placed and written by `nuclear-builder spec new --title … --component … [--layer …]

source, `- Component:`, `- Layer:`, the shape `run.nuc`'s `parseSpec` reads); its folder by component and layer, its

Everything else is the engine's (engine.md): the run file and its log, the station's documents in the spec's folder (`specs/<component>/[<layer>/]<id>/`), the
checks (`checks.json` there, changed only through `nuclear-builder checks`), the exported CI file (`nuclear-builder
export`). Jira's site, email and API token are in VS Code's secret storage (`nuclear.builder.jira`).

the system and the editor keep (2 GB, or 15% of a bigger machine), since it can make the computer freeze or
restart; **tight** when it passes the memory free now (it swaps unless other programs give memory back); else

| `step` | a step ends (`Factory.end`) | `project`, `root`, `spec`, `specTitle`, `run`, `team`, `teamName`, `station`, `step`, `title`, `key`, `actor`, `role`, `member`, `employee`, `agentKind` (local, agent, api), `usage` (null: no provider), `lines` (null: not reported), `result`, `started`, `ended` |

| `run` | a run ends or waits | `result`, `created`, `ended`, `stations` (each `{id, status, started, ended, steps, failed}`), `gates`, `retries`, `costUsd`, `budgetUsd`; the newest line of a run says what it is now |

| `chat` | a chat answer ends (`Chat.done`) | `project`, `root`, `chat`, `team`, `member`, `employee`, `role` (`chat`: the general agent), `channel`, `agentKind`, `usage`, `result` (answered, failed, stopped), `started`, `ended` |
Every line has `v` (1) and `at`. A line that cannot be written never stops a run. The runs a project made before the
ledger are copied into it once (`backfill`, at the first run or `metrics` in that project; `ledger/backfilled.json`
lists the projects copied), with what their files have and `"backfilled": true`. The ledger is the user's: outside the
editors' storage, never sent anywhere.

Three parts, one way: the usage is measured at the source, appended to the factory's ledger, and read by

rows.summary: The Nuclear Developer counts per request (its `TALLY`, a context variable each request sets and every model call adds to; `nuclear-agents/nuclear_developer`); an older Developer gives no `usage`: not reported.
body: The Nuclear Developer counts per request (its `TALLY`, a context variable each request sets and every model call adds
to; `nuclear-agents/nuclear_developer`); an older Developer gives no `usage`: not reported.
A step keeps the sum of its calls as `usage` (`sumUsage`) and the lines it changed as `lines: {added, removed}` (from
the run's `writes`: each write has `added` and `removed`, counted per line as a diff's stat counts them, a moved line
neither). A gate keeps its times in `run.gates` (`{id, kind, station, opened, answered, answer}`). A chat's answer sums
its provider's calls the same way. A run file without these fields (an earlier version) still loads: its steps have no
usage nor lines, and the reports say so.

rows.title: The reports: the usage, the factory's ledger, `metrics` (spec 017) — The usage at the source (`adapter.nuc`)
rows.summary: Every provider's call gives its `Outcome.usage`: `{inTokens, outTokens, costUsd, ms, provider, model}`.
body: Every provider's call gives its `Outcome.usage`: `{inTokens, outTokens, costUsd, ms, provider, model}`. `runAdapter`
stamps the time, the provider and the model (the one the provider said, else the one asked for); each adapter gives
the tokens its provider reports. A count the provider did not report is `null` ("not reported"), never a guess.
| Provider | Tokens in | Tokens out | Model |
| `claude-code` | the result's `usage`: `input_tokens` + `cache_creation_input_tokens` + `cache_read_input_tokens` | `output_tokens` | the `system`/`init` line's `model` |
| `opencode` | each `step_finish`'s `tokens.input` + `cache.read` + `cache.write`, summed | `tokens.output` + `tokens.reasoning` | asked |
| `codex` | each `turn.completed`'s `usage.input_tokens`, summed | `output_tokens` | asked |
| `gemini-cli` | the result's `stats.input_tokens` | `stats.output_tokens` | asked |
| `cursor` | not reported (its `stream-json` has no tokens) | not reported | the `system`/`init` line's `model` |
| `grok` | not reported (its `streaming-json` is not documented) | not reported | asked |
| the APIs | each turn's tokens (the loop of `adapter_api.nuc`), summed | each turn's, summed | asked |
| `nuclear-developer` | the reply's `usage.inTokens` (Ollama's `prompt_eval_count`, summed over the request's model calls) | `usage.outTokens` (`eval_count`) | `usage.model` |

rows.summary: `secret-tool` (Linux), `security` (macOS), the password vault of Windows through PowerShell (`keyringCommand`).
body: - The keys of the `api` providers in the system's keyring, service `nuclear-factory`, attribute `provider`:
`secret-tool` (Linux), `security` (macOS), the password vault of Windows through PowerShell
(`keyringCommand`). The session bus is found when the caller's environment lacks it (`keyringEnv`).
- `factory/vault.json` notes which providers the keyring keeps, never a key. A provider noted that the keyring
does not answer for is a closed keyring: `vaultKey` waits `VAULT_WAIT` (90 s), then refuses. A key is never
written to a file.
- `vault set <provider>` reads the key on stdin (hidden with `getpass` in a terminal), never from the command line;
on macOS `security` takes it as an argument for that instant (a `shortcut:` in the code). `vault remove
<provider>`; `vault list --json` → `{ "<provider>": true | false }`. Nothing prints a key; an API error has the
key replaced by `<key>` (`apiLoop`).

body: Deterministic, no model:
- `team suggest`: each employee against the words of the team's purpose and skills (three letters or more, no
stopword, light stemming: *tests*, *testing* and *tester* meet; five letters or more also meet by prefix). Each word
counts once, by the heaviest source it met: a skill 3, an endorsed skill 2, the headline 2, an experience line, the
profile or the bio 1. The best three of each role (the mean of the stats breaks ties, so a role with no word met
still gets its all-rounders), each with `why`: `[{ "term", "in", "text" }]`, the heaviest first.
- `team name-suggest`: five different names, each a pattern of `team-names.json` in the roles' folder
(`{ "en" | "es": { "patterns", "adj", "noun", "thing", "suffix" } }`, nuclear-agents/roles/README.md) filled at
random; `{topic}` is a word of the purpose, and its patterns are used only with a purpose; `--seed` gives the same
names again.

rows.title: Nuclear Builder: the guides
rows.summary: Nuclear Builder takes a spec through specification, generate, plan, tests first, code, verification, security, artifacts and deploy, on your machine, and shows who did each step.
body: Nuclear Builder takes a spec through specification, generate, plan, tests first, code, verification, security,
artifacts and deploy, on your machine, and shows who did each step. It is the tool *Nuclear Builder* of the Nuclear
workspace in VS Code (`Ctrl+Alt+P`), a tool window in Android Studio / IntelliJ (`Alt+Shift+P`), and the
`nuclear-builder` command in a terminal or a CI job. It needs the Smart Graph and the Nuclear Developer running
([Set up the AI services](../../../../../installer/docs/08-guides/ai-setup.md)).

rows.summary: Nuclear Builder: the guides

| [Write a spec and start the Builder](write-a-spec.md) | write a spec in VS Code, JetBrains or a terminal, and start a run |
| [Follow a run](follow-a-run.md) | follow a run, run something again, read a failure |

rows.title: Ask the team to do it — Any agent, not only the chat
rows.summary: The Builder's tools are an MCP server, `nuclear-builder mcp`.
body: The Builder's tools are an MCP server, `nuclear-builder mcp`. The factory gives it to every agent it runs (Claude
Code, OpenCode, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Grok Build, an API model) beside `nuclear-mcp`. To give it to your own agent in a project:
```sh
claude mcp add nuclear_builder -- nuclear-builder mcp --root /path/to/project
The same rules hold there: a tool that would spend or destroy answers that it waits for you.

rows.title: Ask the team to do it
rows.summary: Everything you can do with the mouse in Nuclear Builder, the team can do from the chat (ADR-platform-0009): read a document, write the specs, start their runs, answer the gates, change a team or the project's line.
body: Everything you can do with the mouse in Nuclear Builder, the team can do from the chat (ADR-platform-0009): read a
document, write the specs, start their runs, answer the gates, change a team or the project's line. You write what
you want in Nuclear Chat; the member that answers uses the Builder's tools, the same commands the page calls
([the list](../02-architecture/actions.md)).

rows.title: Ask the team to do it — From slides to code
rows.summary: 1. Put the document in the project (for example `docs/slides.pdf`).
body: 1. Put the document in the project (for example `docs/slides.pdf`). The team reads a PDF (with `pdftotext`, from
poppler-utils: if the machine has none, it says so), a PowerPoint `.pptx`, markdown and any text. A `.ppt`, `.key`
or `.odp` is refused: save it as PDF or `.pptx` first.
2. In the team's channel (or `general`), write:
> read docs/slides.pdf and write all the specs from those slides, then write the code through the Builder
3. The member reads the slides, writes one spec per feature with its acceptance criteria (a spec without criteria
cannot run: when the slides do not say how to check a feature, it asks you), then starts their runs. Each run is
told in its own thread, station by station.
4. The runs stop at their gates (the Analysis, the Design, the Delivery by default): approve, ask for a change or
leave it for later with the thread's buttons, on the Builder's page, or by telling the member ("approve the
design of lend-a-book").

rows.title: Ask the team to do it — What the team never decides alone
rows.summary: or the two in the editor when you press Resume on the Builder's page.
body: - **Money**: a run (or a member) with a paid provider waits for your two confirmations: two questions in the chat,
or the two in the editor when you press Resume on the Builder's page. *Force confirmation* keeps working: the team
can never answer them.
- **What destroys or acts in your name**: deleting a spec or a team, running a run again from scratch, the pull
request of the Delivery (a commit in your name), the line's gates, commands and *force confirmation*, replacing a
CI file. The member asks you in the chat (yes or no); nothing changes until you say yes.
- **Merging** a pull request: never.

rows.title: Follow a run — It survives the editor, and it keeps working
rows.summary: Code closes or crashes in the middle, the run is found interrupted when it opens again, what was left half written is undone, and it goes on from that station (`nuclear.builder.resumeInterrupted`).
body: - A run is a process of `nuclear-builder`, with a trace log, a heartbeat and a ledger of the files it writes. If VS
Code closes or crashes in the middle, the run is found interrupted when it opens again, what was left half written
is undone, and it goes on from that station (`nuclear.builder.resumeInterrupted`). Two windows never run the same
run. *Stop* interrupts a run that works (what its working steps wrote is undone) and leaves one that waits waiting.
- Every run first checks its connections (the Developer, the graph, Ollama and the local roles' models, each agent's
command, a key in the vault for each API provider, the MCP server, free disk).
- A run does not stop when you switch tools or close its page. A notification, and a badge on the Nuclear icon,
tell you when it waits for you and when it ends.
- *Settings and integrations* (`Ctrl+Alt+S`) holds the services, the local models, the MCP server for Claude Code,
Codex and Cursor, the connections and the retries.

rows.title: Follow a run — Run anything again
rows.summary: before it are kept.
body: - *Run <station> again*, on every station and every step: it and every station after it run again; the stations
before it are kept.
- *Run again from scratch*, on the run: every station from the Analysis.
What the steps left out wrote is undone first. A file you changed since the run wrote it is kept, and the page says
so. The attempt left behind stays under the run with its reason. A run made by the earlier engine can only run again
from scratch.
```sh
nuclear-builder retry <run> [--from <station>]
nuclear-builder restart <run>
Over MCP: `developer_retry`.

rows.title: Follow a run — The diagram of a run
rows.summary: who does their work; the providers in use (on this machine and free, or paid, with the run's budget); the Smart Graph and GitHub.
body: - **Context** (where a run opens): the project in the middle; you; the team's members who work the run with their avatars and names and
who does their work; the providers in use (on this machine and free, or paid, with the run's budget); the Smart
Graph and GitHub. The edges say who talks to whom, and flow while they do: the role working and its provider, the
project asking you when a station waits.
- **Stations**: a node per station, left to right (Analysis → Design → Tests first → Code → Quality → Delivery), with
the employee and the provider and model that work it, its state, time, progress and the step on now. A light runs
round the station working, one that waits for you breathes in amber, and the edge that hands the work to it flows.
The view opens on the station working (or waiting, or failed) and its neighbours.
- **Inside a station** (its *⤢ Inside* or a double click): its steps with the employee and model that did each, and
under each step the steps its agent followed, the last one lit while it works. The stations before and after stand
at the sides.

rows.title: Follow a run — The strategy of a request
rows.summary: fixes first (`nuclear fix .`), then each file with errors is repaired with the card of each error.
body: - **The stations that run.** A compile error skips the generators, the plan and *Tests first*: the compiler's exact
fixes first (`nuclear fix .`), then each file with errors is repaired with the card of each error. A failing test
goes straight to *Quality*. A rename plans and writes, and writes no test.
- **Where the pieces come from.** For a new feature the planner splits what the generators left. For a change of
something that exists (a field more, a column) the pieces are the files that declare it. For a rename a tool
gives every file that writes the name, already rewritten: no model writes.
- **What is asked first.** A stored resource without its fields, a rename without its two names, a bug without what
should happen: the analysis stops the run with the question. Nothing is guessed.
- **The wiring.** After *Code*, each use case the coder wrote is wired by `nuclear gen usecase`: its alias in the
facade and, when the spec's sentence gives it (`POST orders/{id}/cancel`), its route.
- **A bug's repair** goes to the file the failure names, whoever wrote it, and never to the test.
A request that is not a run (a question, a command, something beyond the platform) stops at the analysis and says
where it belongs. When the analysis read it wrong, name the strategy in the spec (`- Strategy: usecase`, under
`- Use case:`) and run it again.

rows.title: Follow a run — The strategy of a request
rows.summary: What a strategy changes in a run:
body: | Family | Kinds of request |

| create | a whole system, a visual prototype with fixed data, a project, a component, a resource of another API, a stored resource, the app of a backend, only an interface, a repository, a use case, a route, one declaration |
| change | one more field, method or action; a rename; a move or an extraction; a break of the architecture's rules; the database's schema; the configuration; taking something out |
| fix | it does not compile; a test fails; it does the wrong thing; it fails while running; the data does not match; a screen shows the wrong thing; the machine or a service fails |
| verify and explain | tests for what exists; a security review; documentation; a question; building, running and shipping |
| beyond | what NuclearLang or the local agents cannot do: said before anything is written |
What a strategy changes in a run:

rows.title: Follow a run — The strategy of a request
rows.summary: A whole system, one screen, a rename and a failing test are not done the same way.
body: A whole system, one screen, a rename and a failing test are not done the same way. The graph holds a **strategy**
for each kind of request (33 rows, `strategy:<name>`; ADR-developer-0001): how the kind is recognised, its plan with the
tool of every step, and what it asks of a run. The local **analyst** picks it before anything is generated or
planned (its first step). No model chooses: the request's exact signs decide (a diagnostic code, a test's output, `rename A to B`, a
`GET <url>` line), then its meaning, and whether the project already has the names it writes.

rows.summary: exponential backoff; the settings say how many times and how long.
body: - A call to the local agents that fails for a passing reason (the service starting, busy, a 5xx) is retried with
exponential backoff; the settings say how many times and how long. Each retry is in the step's trace.
- When a station fails, the local diagnoser tells why and what to do (its *Why it failed* step). *↻ Run <station>
again* (or `nuclear-builder retry <run>`) runs it again from there, keeping every station that passed.

On the page, the diagram with Nuclear Chat under it; on the right, above, **the node**; below, **the log**, with the

3. **Suggested members**: for each role, the employees whose profile fits the purpose and skills, with why (the

Run it to see what the server will see before you push.

rows.title: The pipeline's commands, locally and on a server
rows.summary: CLI (`nuclear check`, `nuclear build`, `install`, `test`).
body: *Pipeline settings* opens `.nuclear/builder.json`, the commands of each stage. The defaults come from the platform's

deploy stage:
```json
"commands": {
"seed": ["nuclear migrate", "python seed.py"],
"integration": ["nuclear test -- -m integration"],
"deploy": ["docker compose up -d --build"]
"branches": ["main", "feature/**"]
A project's `.nuclear/builder.json` wins over the editor's `nuclear.ai.*` settings for its own pipeline: it is shared

rows.title: The pipeline's commands, locally and on a server — The software factory's line
rows.summary: `nuclear-builder run` (in a terminal, a CI job or the JetBrains window) runs the software factory: the spec through Analysis, Design, Tests first, Code, Quality and Delivery, each station worked by a member of its role in your team (the one `--assign` names, else the role's first)…
body: `nuclear-builder run` (in a terminal, a CI job or the JetBrains window) runs the software factory: the spec through
Analysis, Design, Tests first, Code, Quality and Delivery, each station worked by a member of its role in your team (the one `--assign` names, else the role's first)
(`nuclear-builder team list`). The same `.nuclear/builder.json` holds the rest of the line:
```json
"team": "night-shift",
"gates": ["analysis", "design", "delivery"],
"stations": ["analysis", "design", "tests", "code", "quality", "delivery"],
"forceConfirm": false,
"prices": { "openai/<model>": [1.25, 10] }
- A gate stops the run for you: approve, ask for a change, or stop; `nuclear-builder run --resume <id>` asks again.
- Paid providers (an agent's command line, an API model) are confirmed twice before the first call, or in advance
with `--confirm-spending`, which `"forceConfirm": true` refuses. The team's budget (5 USD by default) holds for
the whole run.
- QA's plan is the run's checks: `nuclear-builder checks <id>` lists them; `add --title … --station …`, `on`/`off`
and `mark <check> passed|failed` change them.
- DevOps, at the Delivery station, opens the pull request only when you approve it, from the branch `factory/<id>`, with your git identity.

body: ```sh
nuclear-builder metrics                                   # the bill and the main numbers
nuclear-builder metrics --team red --by week --json       # every report of a team, by week
nuclear-builder metrics --view people --from 2026-11-01   # each member's work since a date
An agent asks the same with the MCP tool `metrics` ("how much did the team spend this week?").

rows.title: Read what the factory spent and made — In VS Code
rows.summary: Open Reports on the Nuclear workspace's strip (the bar chart with a coin, `Ctrl+Alt+K`), or the command *Builder Reports: What the Factory Spent and Made*.
body: Open **Reports** on the Nuclear workspace's strip (the bar chart with a coin, `Ctrl+Alt+K`), or the command *Builder
Reports: What the Factory Spent and Made*.
- **The bill**, on top: tokens in and out, the money spent, local against paid, the budget the runs used, and tokens
and money by day or week.
- **The tabs**, the reports of a sprint: *Throughput* (specs delivered by period, velocity by team), *Cycle time*
(each spec from its run's start to its delivery, and the time per station), *Burndown* (the period's specs left and
delivered), *Flow* (where the specs were at the end of each period), *Waiting for you* (the gates open now and how
long), *Quality* (failures, retries and the first-try pass rate per station), *People* (each member's work, ranked
by cost or by result) and *Indicators* (cost per delivered spec, tokens per useful line, the local share).
- **The filters**: a project, a team, a member, the dates, by day or by week.
A member's numbers are also in their panel's **Summary** on *Your software company*; its *Reports* button opens the
page filtered to them.

rows.title: Read what the factory spent and made
rows.summary: Every step of a run and every answer of Nuclear Chat writes one line in your factory's ledger (`~/.config/nuclearlang/factory/ledger/`, on your machine only): who did it (the team, the member, the role), where (the project, the spec, the station or the channel), the tokens and the money the…
body: Every step of a run and every answer of Nuclear Chat writes one line in your factory's ledger
(`~/.config/nuclearlang/factory/ledger/`, on your machine only): who did it (the team, the member, the role), where
(the project, the spec, the station or the channel), the tokens and the money the provider reported, the time, the
lines of code it added and removed, and whether it passed. The reports read that ledger, for every project of the
machine.

rows.title: Read what the factory spent and made — What the numbers mean
rows.summary: Codex's and Gemini CLI's turns, the APIs' usage, Ollama's counts for the local agents).
body: - **Measured, never estimated.** The tokens are the provider's own counts (Claude Code's usage, OpenCode's steps,
Codex's and Gemini CLI's turns, the APIs' usage, Ollama's counts for the local agents). A provider that reports none
(Cursor and Grok Build today) is counted as *not reported*, not as a guess.
- **Local against paid**: the local agents cost nothing in money; their tokens and time are still counted.
- **Runs of before**: the runs a project made before this version are copied into the ledger once, with what their
files had (their money and times; no tokens nor lines).

rows.title: Write a spec and start the Builder — 1. Set up once
rows.summary: curl -fsSL https://nuclearlang.github.io/install.sh | sh # NuclearLang, then the set-up of the AI services nuclear-builder setup # the set-up alone, any time The set-up reads your machine, suggests a set of models that fits it (`lite`, `medium` or `hard`, or remote agents only), says how far each…
body: ```sh
curl -fsSL https://nuclearlang.github.io/install.sh | sh    # NuclearLang, then the set-up of the AI services
nuclear-builder setup                                           # the set-up alone, any time
The set-up reads your machine, suggests a set of models that fits it (`lite`, `medium` or `hard`, or remote agents
only), says how far each works, and installs what you choose: the Smart Graph, the Nuclear Developer, the models,
the knowledge base. Both services then start at every login. VS Code has the same set-up as a wizard (*Nuclear: Set
Up the AI Services*). Every step, the profiles and what to do when one fails:
[Set up the AI services](../../../../../installer/docs/08-guides/ai-setup.md).
```sh
nuclear-builder setup --status                              # what is installed and running
nuclear-builder team list --json                            # your teams (the company screen makes them)
No program can read the graph until you allow it with `connect` or `allow` (the set-up allows the Developer and the
MCP server). Its documents are encrypted on disk and it refuses web pages
([the Smart Graph](../../../../../nuclear-graph-storage/README.md)).

rows.title: Write a spec and start the Builder — 3. Without VS Code
rows.summary: specs and runs.
body: - **JetBrains** (Android Studio, IntelliJ): the *Nuclear Builder* tool window (`Alt+Shift+P`) lists every project's
specs and runs. *New Spec* writes the file, *Run the Spec with a Team…* runs it with the team you choose, and each

`nuclear-builder runs`.
- **A frontier model over MCP**: the Nuclear MCP server tells every frontier model to generate first
(`generate_resource`, `generate_usecase`) and to let the local developer work on what is left. `developer_task`
runs this pipeline with the local agents and answers the journal; the frontier model validates (`nuclear_check`,
`nuclear test`), corrects only what is wrong and records it with `developer_review`, whose corrected files
become examples in the graph for the local developer ([the MCP server](../../../../../tools/mcp/AGENTS.md)).
Every run is kept in `.nuclear/builder/runs/<id>.json`, the same file each editor draws.

rows.summary: A spec is a markdown file in the same shape, in the folder of its business component: `specs/<component>/<id>/spec.md`, `specs/<component>/<layer>/<id>/spec.md` when it touches one layer (`presentation`, `domain`, `data`), `specs/_global/<id>/spec.md` for the whole project.
body: A spec is a markdown file in the same shape, in the folder of its business component:
`specs/<component>/<id>/spec.md`, `specs/<component>/<layer>/<id>/spec.md` when it touches one layer
(`presentation`, `domain`, `data`), `specs/_global/<id>/spec.md` for the whole project. `nuclear-builder spec new`
writes its base there:
```sh
nuclear-builder spec new --title "Book a room" --component booking --layer domain --description "A guest books a free room."
nuclear-builder spec list                         # the specs by component and layer
nuclear-builder spec move <id> --component rooms  # a spec to another component or layer, its run with it
nuclear-builder spec migrate                      # the specs of the earlier flat specs/<id>/ to their component
nuclear-builder spec accept <id>                  # a member's draft (spec.draft.md) over the spec; discard <id> drops it

rows.title: Write a spec and start the Builder — 4. Name the resources and let the generators write them
rows.summary: In *Design*, the generators come before the Architect.
body: In *Design*, the generators come before the Architect. `nuclear gen resource` writes, already compiling:
- every resource the spec names: a `## Resources` section with one `nuclear gen resource` argument line per item,
or else each `GET <url>` line of the description (`GET https://rickandmortyapi.com/api/character` is
`characters Character`);
- every resource the analysis read in plain words ("each supplier has a name and a phone; we add and list them").
Each call is tried with `--dry-run` first. The fields come from the spec's example answer or its `Key | Type`
table, or from the API's own answer. The Architect then plans only what is left, often nothing.

rows.title: Backend engineer — How you work
rows.summary: 1. Start from the platform, not from memory: call `nuclear_start` on the Nuclear MCP server (or run `nuclear help start`), then read `nuclear spec --brief --dialect <dialect>` and `nuclear help backend`.
body: 1. Start from the platform, not from memory: call `nuclear_start` on the Nuclear MCP server (or run
`nuclear help start`), then read `nuclear spec --brief --dialect <dialect>` and `nuclear help backend`. Look up
every word you are not sure of with `nuclear help <word> --dialect <dialect>`; never guess a syntax.
2. With the local AI services, ask `graph_strategy` for the plan of the request.
3. Inspect before writing: `nuclear gen inspect` (MCP `project_inspect`).
4. Generate first: `nuclear gen resource` for each resource, `nuclear gen usecase` for each use case that only
calls a repository or needs wiring, `nuclear make <kind> <component> <Name>` for each other piece.
5. Write by hand only what no generator knows, in Nuclear: a use case's rules, a query, a tool's doc comment.
With the local developer running, hand that part to `developer_task`, then review what it wrote.
6. Test first for each criterion (skill `tdd`), then `nuclear check . --json` until it prints `[]`,
`nuclear install` once, and `nuclear test` until green.
7. For schema changes: `nuclear migrate make "<message>"`, read the migration, `nuclear migrate`.
8. Update the project's `AGENTS.md`, `docs/` and roadmap in the same change.

rows.title: QA and security tester — How you work
rows.summary: 1. Read the spec and the change.
body: 1. Read the spec and the change. Learn the platform from itself: `nuclear_start` on the Nuclear MCP server (or
`nuclear help start`), the platform's topic (`nuclear help backend|mobile|web`), and each word with
`nuclear help <word> --dialect <dialect>`.
2. Run the tools first: `nuclear check . --json` (`[]`), `nuclear fmt --check .`, `nuclear test`, or the whole line
with `nuclear-builder ci check test security`.
3. Plan the checks: each criterion, then empty, missing, repeated, limits, wrong types, unknown ids, another user's
item, no permission, concurrent requests, a dependency down. In a factory run, keep them in
`nuclear-builder checks <id>`.
4. Write the missing tests in `test/<name>_test.nuc` (backend `appClient()` for statuses and guards; `@states` and
`@widget` on mobile and web). A test you write must fail when the rule is broken.
5. Review security (skill `security-review-owasp`); MCP `developer_security` helps on a single piece.
6. Measure the changed paths with `nuclear run --monitor` and `nuclear monitor` when performance matters.
7. Report: each finding with file and line, how to reproduce it (the test), the risk, and the fix in Nuclear.

rows.title: Nuclear Developer — Why
rows.summary: Why
body: - A frontier model doing a whole spec is paid per token, and the code leaves the machine.
- So the lead (Claude, or you) decides; the local developer writes each piece; what it cannot fix becomes an example in the graph.
- Left out on purpose: only Nuclear for a platform, never a dialect; nothing a tool can write.

rows.title: Vision — Problem
rows.summary: A frontier model that does all the work of a spec is paid for every token, and the code leaves the machine.
body: A frontier model that does all the work of a spec is paid for every token, and the code leaves the machine. A model
small enough to run on a developer's laptop (at most 3B parameters) cannot hold much context, chooses tools badly,
and the machine has no GPU to train one.
The Nuclear Developer is a set of local agents for NuclearLang and Synapsis that work as **the junior developer of
a frontier model**: a lead (Claude, or the user) makes the decisions (the plan, the names, the review) and the
local developer writes each piece. What a small model cannot hold in its head comes from the
[Nuclear Smart Graph](../../../../nuclear-graph-storage/README.md); what it writes is checked by the Nuclear
compiler before it answers. What the junior cannot fix, the lead fixes and keeps as an example in the graph, so the
junior gets it right next time.

rows.title: Vision — The idea behind the design
rows.summary: (recall, write, check, repair), never a model with a toolbox.
body: - **A small model follows fixed steps better than it chooses tools.** Each agent is a graph with fixed steps
(recall, write, check, repair), never a model with a toolbox.
- **Tools before models.** A generator writes what is standard, the compiler's exact fixes come before any repair,
a rename is done by a tool: a model writes only a piece of one file that no tool can write.
- **The agents are trained by retrieval and distillation**, not by changing weights: a failure is fixed with a
general rule or more knowledge in the graph, never with the answer.

rows.title: Vision — What it does not do
rows.summary: `web`), never a dialect.
body: - It does not choose names, data or architecture: the order gives them.
- It does not write a target language. The agents write only Nuclear: they name a platform (`backend`, `mobile`,
`web`), never a dialect.
- It does not run a model larger than 3B parameters of effective size (the user's rule).
- Its assistant does not change a file: an order is a run of the Builder.
- It does not hide what is beyond it: the plan and the analysis say so before anything is written
([the limits](../02-architecture/overview.md#known-limits)).

rows.title: Vision — Who uses it
rows.summary: security and artifacts with the local agents.
body: - **The Builder** of the editors and `nuclear-builder`: a spec goes through plan, tests first, code, verification,
security and artifacts with the local agents.
- **Nuclear Atlas** of the editor: a question about the project, or an order.
- **A frontier model** over MCP (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor): `developer_task` first, then it validates and
corrects.
How each calls it: [integrations](../02-architecture/integrations.md#where-it-works).

rows.title: Integrations and contracts — The HTTP API
rows.summary: a dialect's name) is refused with 400 (the validation error, naming the field) before an agent runs (it was a 500 from the graph's `/v1/kinds/`).
body: - `platform` is `backend`, `mobile` or `web`: the agents name a platform, never a dialect. Any other value (`""`,
a dialect's name) is refused with 400 (the validation error, naming the field) before an agent runs (it was a 500 from the graph's `/v1/kinds/`).
- `root` is the project's folder: with it an agent reads the project by itself.
- `query` (chat): the developer's own words when `message` is a whole prompt of its own (Nuclear Builder's chat
member: who it is, its tools, the conversation). The graph (two cards instead of four) and the project's files are
searched with them, and the assistant's guide is left out: the prompt brings its own.
- `trace` is the steps the agent followed, with what it read.
- `usage` is what the request's models read and wrote, as Ollama counted them: `{inTokens, outTokens, model}` (the
sums of `prompt_eval_count` and `eval_count` over every model call of the request, the last model that answered);
empty when no model reported counts. Each request counts its own (`TALLY` of `workbench.nuc`, a context variable
the controller sets per request; a graph's steps share it). Nuclear Builder keeps it in its ledger (spec 017).
- The analysis runs before a run generates or plans anything: [strategies.md](strategies.md).

rows.title: Integrations and contracts — The HTTP API
body: On `127.0.0.1:7879`. Every route is `POST /developer/<name>` and answers `200`.
| Route | Request | Answer |
| `code`, `test`, `security` | `{task, platform = "backend", path, kind, context, root}` | `{code, report, check, attempts, trace: [{step, detail}], usage}` |
| `document` | the same; the run's journal in `context` | the same; the summary in `report` |
| `diagnose` | the same; `task` is the step, `context` its output, `path` the project's folder | the same |
| `accept` | the same; `task` the criteria, numbered; `context` the facts and the files of the run | the same |
| `chat` | `{message, platform, map, history, root, query}` | the same answer (`report`) |
| `plan` | `{spec, platform, root}` | `{pieces: [{path, kind, task}], raw, trace, tree, limits, usage}` |
| `analyze` | `{spec, platform, root, strategy}` | `{strategy, title, why, mode, stages, lead, source, generate, pieces, questions, limits, report, trace, usage}` |

| Ollama | the two models, and the chat's own | `OLLAMA_URL`, `CODER_MODEL`, `ASSISTANT_MODEL`, `CONTEXT_TOKENS`, `CHAT_MODEL`, `CHAT_CONTEXT_TOKENS`, `CHAT_KEEP_ALIVE` |

rows.title: Integrations and contracts — Where it works
rows.summary: Where it works
body: | Who calls it | How | What the Developer does |

| The **Builder** (VS Code `Ctrl+Alt+P`, Android Studio *Nuclear Builder*, `nuclear-builder run`) | spec → plan → tests first → code → verification → security → artifacts → deploy | the planner splits the spec, the tester writes the tests first (and fixes a test file the project rejects), the coder writes each piece and repairs it with the compiler and with failing tests told in Nuclear (`nuclear explain`), the security reviewer reads each new file; when a stage fails the **diagnoser** says why; at the end the **documenter** writes the journal's summary |
| **Nuclear Atlas** (VS Code `Ctrl+Alt+A`) | a question, or `/task <order>` | the **assistant** answers from the project's map and the graph; an order is a Builder run with the local agents only |

| A **frontier model** over MCP (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor: `nuclear-mcp`) | `developer_task` first, then validate, correct, `developer_review`; `developer_retry` after a failure | the whole task by the local agents (`nuclear-builder run --lead local`), documented in the run's journal; the lead's corrected files become graph examples |

rows.title: Integrations and contracts — Where it works
rows.summary: a ledger of the files it writes; an orphaned run is recovered (its unfinished step's files undone) and goes on from that step.
body: **When the editor closes in the middle.** A run keeps a trace log (`.nuclear/builder/runs/<id>.log`), a heartbeat and
a ledger of the files it writes; an orphaned run is recovered (its unfinished step's files undone) and goes on from
that step. A call to the Developer nothing works on (the Developer silent, Ollama holding no model) is cut and
retried, and every run first checks that the Developer, the graph, Ollama and the models it needs answer.

rows.title: Integrations and contracts — Where it works
rows.summary: The Builder, Nuclear Atlas and `nuclear-builder` are the project `extensions/`; the MCP tools (`developer_task`, `developer_retry`, `developer_review`, `developer_code`, `developer_test`, `developer_security`) are the project `tools/mcp`.
body: The Builder, Nuclear Atlas and `nuclear-builder` are the project [`extensions/`](../../../../extensions/AGENTS.md); the MCP
tools (`developer_task`, `developer_retry`, `developer_review`, `developer_code`, `developer_test`,
`developer_security`) are the project [`tools/mcp`](../../../../tools/mcp/AGENTS.md).
**Every run is documented.** `.nuclear/builder/runs/<id>.md` (beside the `.json` with every log whole): the
documenter's summary (what it built, how it checked it, what is left), why it failed (the diagnoser), the files
written, what is left for the reviewer, and each step with its agent, its trace and what it read; a frontier
model's review is `<id>.review.md`.
**When something fails.** A call to the Developer that fails for a passing reason (down, busy, 408/425/429/5xx) is
retried by its caller with exponential backoff and full jitter (5 tries, 1–30 s by default; `Retry-After` wins). A
compiler error or a failing test is never retried blindly: it goes to the repair rounds, then to the diagnoser
(kind by rules: transient, environment, code, test, spec; evidence from `nuclear check` or `nuclear doctor`; the
next step). A failed run goes on from the step that failed (*↻ Retry*, `nuclear-builder retry <run>`,
`developer_retry`): every step that passed is kept, the earlier attempt stays in the run file.

rows.title: Architecture
rows.summary: The Nuclear Developer is itself a Synapsis backend written in Nuclear (platform `backend`, dialect `fastapi`): FastAPI + LangGraph, generated from the `.nuc` files of this folder.
body: The Nuclear Developer is itself a Synapsis backend written in Nuclear (platform `backend`, dialect `fastapi`):
FastAPI + LangGraph, generated from the `.nuc` files of this folder. It listens on `127.0.0.1:7879`.

rows.title: Architecture — How an agent works
rows.summary: many.
body: many. How people write a kind ("application component", "use case") comes from the graph's cards of the kinds.
- **The plan knows the project.** With the project's folder (`root`), a declaration the project already has and the
spec only uses (`repository: BookRepository`) is not planned again; one the spec introduces with its kind's word
("a repository BookRepository with...") is planned as a change of its file; and new pieces go to the component of
the declarations the spec uses, whatever component the model names.
The whole toolbox of an agent is one row of the graph, `service:agent-toolbox`: the graph, the compiler, the
`nuclear` commands, the project's files and the internet.

rows.title: Architecture — How an agent works
rows.summary: A small model follows fixed steps better than it chooses tools, so each agent is a LangGraph graph with fixed steps: recall ──► write ──► nuclear check ──ok──► answer │ ▲ │ │ └── repair ◄─┘ errors (at most 3 attempts), each with the card of its code └─ from the Smart Graph, for the kind it is…
body: A small model follows fixed steps better than it chooses tools, so each agent is a LangGraph graph with fixed steps:
recall ──► write ──► nuclear check ──ok──► answer
│          └── repair ◄─┘ errors (at most 3 attempts), each with the card of its code
└─ from the Smart Graph, for the kind it is about to write: the kind's own card, the mistakes
small models repeat with that kind, the closest rules, solved tasks and an example file
More happens by rule, never by the model's choice:

rows.title: Architecture — How an agent works
rows.summary: its context, the files that declare the names its task writes (`Workspace.context`, read-only, never outside the project), besides what the caller pasted.
body: - **It reads the project by itself.** A request may carry `root` (the project's folder): the coder then gets, as
its context, the files that declare the names its task writes (`Workspace.context`, read-only, never outside the
project), besides what the caller pasted. An order can be short: the path, the kind, every name.
- **Its answer is held to the order's own words.** When the answer compiles, the quoted texts, the decorators with
their arguments, the calls (`books.byAuthor(name)`), the signatures (also the ones without parameters, `all()`)
and the status codes the task writes must be in it. What is missing is asked for once more, without the examples
(`agents/faithful.md`), and the first answer is kept when the second is not better. It exists for the short
orders of a lead, where a renamed call breaks the next piece.
- **The plan says what is beyond the agents.** `POST /developer/plan` answers the pieces, the same plan as a tree
(`tree`: the big parts, one per component; the tasks of each, a layer; the pieces of each task, a file) and
`limits`: the rows of the graph's capabilities whose trigger words the spec writes ("authentication" on the
backend, "form" on the web), a spec longer than a local model reads at once, a plan without pieces or with too

rows.title: Architecture — Known limits
rows.summary: The agents know their own limits: they are rows of the graph (`limit:agent-one-file`, `limit:agent-context`, `limit:agent-reasoning`, `limit:agent-features`, `limit:agent-nuclear-only`, `limit:agent-internet`) with the procedure to follow when a task is beyond them (`playbook:escalate`).
body: The agents know their own limits: they are rows of the graph (`limit:agent-one-file`, `limit:agent-context`,
`limit:agent-reasoning`, `limit:agent-features`, `limit:agent-nuclear-only`, `limit:agent-internet`) with the
procedure to follow when a task is beyond them (`playbook:escalate`).

rows.title: Architecture — Known limits
rows.summary: model got a test of an application component from the examples): the run fails at *Tests first* with the diagnosis instead of passing without tests; Claude-led runs fix it.
body: - The 3B tester copies a solved example of the graph when it is close to the task (a spec that declares only a
model got a test of an application component from the examples): the run fails at *Tests first* with the
diagnosis instead of passing without tests; Claude-led runs fix it.
- The planner maps a kind only from its own word ("application component" is not `appcomponent`) and names a
component after the first model of a plain spec (`newbooks`).
- A value that comes from a library method has no known type: declare it (`card: string = ~knowledge.card(...)`)
before using a member of the standard library on it.
- The coder's and the assistant's connections set no limit on the length of an answer (the chat's does: 1024
tokens): a model that enters an answer without end holds the Developer and every call after it until the process
is killed. Seen with `qwen2.5-coder:3b` as assistant, `llama3.2:1b` and `phi3:3.8b`; the evaluation has no watch
on a call that stalls.
- On features of several files written by the local agents alone, a piece renames a method the spec writes, or two
pieces declare the same thing. That is why a feature goes through the generators first and, when it has a design
of its own, under a lead.
What is being done about them: [the roadmap](../01-product/roadmap.md).

rows.title: Architecture — The agents
rows.summary: The agents
body: | Diagnoser | `gemma4:e2b` | `POST /developer/diagnose` | when a pipeline stage fails: the kind of failure by fixed rules (transient, environment, code, test, spec), the evidence from the tools (`nuclear check`, `nuclear doctor`) and the next step in plain words | change anything |

| Acceptor | `gemma4:e2b` | `POST /developer/accept` | after a run's verification passes: holds each acceptance criterion against what the run left (its files, its tests, the commands that passed) and says which are shown met, with the evidence | fail a run (its verdict is for the reviewer) |

| Planner | `gemma4:e2b` | `POST /developer/plan` | splits a spec into pieces of one file, in order; each path comes from the platform's layout (`nuclear help layout`), each kind and forgotten piece from the spec's own words | choose a folder, or plan what the spec does not name |

| Analyst | `gemma4:e2b`, for one question only | `POST /developer/analyze` | before a run generates or plans anything: which kind of request the spec is, the stages that run, the generator calls, the pieces the tools give, the questions ([strategies.md](strategies.md)) | choose the strategy by a model, or guess a missing fact |

rows.title: Architecture — The agents
rows.summary: The agents
body: | Agent | Model | Route | Does | Does not |
| Coder | `qwen2.5-coder:3b` | `POST /developer/code` | writes ONE `.nuc` file from a precise task, repairs it with the compiler | choose names, data or architecture |
| Tester | `qwen2.5-coder:3b` | `POST /developer/test` | writes the Nuclear tests (`tests` kind) of a piece of code | delete a failing test |
| Security | `gemma4:e2b` | `POST /developer/security` | reviews code against the platform's security rules + the compiler | change the code |

| Assistant | `qwen3.5:2b` (the chat's own model) | `POST /developer/chat` | answers a message of the editor's chat about the project, from the project's map, the session's last messages and the graph; a question with one right answer (which, how many, what are) gets the rows of the graph's exact facts, which end the answer as they are (`ADR-graph-0002`) | change a file (an order is a Builder run) |
